The drawing routine, OR for side-on and level, slanted otherwise, mirrored for the other side, is written into the JSR at $7DA1. A crashing helicopter is clipped at the bottom by its crash step, so it sinks into the ground.
gfx_place's inline argument (the call at $7D86): the address of the place to draw at, place_x ($001C-$001E: the world X, low and high, and the row).
The body's shape, by the pose and tilt.
gfx_shape's inline argument (the call at $7D8B): the address of the shape's pointer, shape_ptr ($001A), which the code above has just set.
Clips the body to the window; while the helicopter is crashing, its crash step cuts rows off its bottom as it sinks into the ground.
gfx_clip's inline arguments (the call at $7D9A), the clip's margins in dots and rows: the left margin 0, the right margin 0, the top margin 0.
The bottom margin of the gfx_clip call, rewritten with the crash step.
The JSR whose address ($7DA2/$7DA3) draw_heli writes: gfx_draw_or ($1021), its mirror ($1024), gfx_draw_slant ($1033) or its mirror ($1036). As loaded it reads JSR $FFFF.
The low byte of heli_draw_call's address, written by draw_heli for the pose.
The high byte of heli_draw_call's address, $10.
The drawing routine for each pose, -5 to +5, when the helicopter is tilted: the mirrored OR for -5, the mirrored slant for -4 to -1, the slant for 0 to 4, the OR for 5.
The high bytes of heli_draw_table's addresses, all $10.

Draws the main rotor, sheared by the tilt, at an offset from the body's place given by the table at $6D51 (11 tilts by 11 poses) plus the one at $6E43 (by tilt). It turns through three pictures ($A024), one a frame, and stops when the helicopter crashes.
gfx_place's inline argument (the call at $7DFD): the address of the place to draw at, place_x ($001C-$001E: the world X, low and high, and the row).
Slants the rotor by the helicopter's tilt and steps the rotor's picture on, 4, 2, 0, unless it is crashing.
gfx_shape's inline argument (the call at $7E2C): the address of the shape's pointer, shape_ptr ($001A), which the code above has just set.
Clips the main rotor to the window and draws it slanted.
The rotor's picture, 4, 2, 0, 4...: an offset into $A024.

Draws the tail rotor. Facing the viewer, or one step from it and tilted away, every other frame it is a dot two rows tall (the shape at $7EE4) at the offset for the tilt from the table at $6E59. Side-on it turns through four pictures ($A02A) at the offset for the tilt from $6E6F, or $6E85 for the other side, and stops when the helicopter crashes. Between, none is drawn.
gfx_place's inline argument (the call at $7E72): the address of the place to draw at, place_x ($001C-$001E: the world X, low and high, and the row).
The end-on tail rotor's shape, given directly by the two bytes after the call: $7EE4.

Here the jet's code doubles as data: the noise routine ($76E3) reads the delay before each pair of clicks from $8101 onwards, the bytes of the instructions that follow. The code: in manoeuvres 1 and 2 the jet's height closes on the helicopter's, then the manoeuvre's routine.

Manoeuvre 0, cruising. A jet leaves (the last five steps of manoeuvre 4, climbing away) once the helicopter has been hit, once it is over the fence's block or beyond, or when it is more than two blocks from the helicopter. Within 152 dots (plus 4 a level), a bold jet ($80) swoops (manoeuvre 2); the others turn round to attack (manoeuvre 1) when flying away from the helicopter, and when coming at it, turn or swoop once it is within 64 dots and moving at 9 dots a frame or more. Further off they act only when the helicopter comes at them at 20 dots a frame or more (15 for a bold jet).

Manoeuvres 3 and 4, the attack run: at its first step manoeuvre 3 fires two missiles ($8B5F) and manoeuvre 4 drops a bomb ($8BF2). At its last step the jet stays there until it is off the screen, then leaves the jet list and frees its slot.

Below height 4 it hits the ground: at depth 3 it is simply dropped; otherwise it explodes there ($8634) and its blast does its harm ($881D). What a flying shot hits. At the ground's depth and lower than 14, within 24 dots right of a barracks' X, it explodes against it (and the blast can open it, $88AD). Higher than 24 it can hit a jet that has come forward to within 8 rows of the ground's depth: within 8 rows of its height and 19 dots of its X; at any height, a drone within 8 rows and 16 dots. Either is destroyed ($8A0B, $8A9F) and the shot becomes an explosion.
A missile within 9 rows and 10 dots of the helicopter explodes, at one row in front of the ground's depth, and the helicopter is hit ($8924).
A drone within 7 rows and 18 dots of the helicopter is taken off the drone list and explodes, and the helicopter is hit.

The harm an explosion does where it lands, nothing in the base's block or beyond. At the ground's depth or behind it: a helicopter on the ground within 11 dots is hit ($8924); every hostage within about 10 dots that is not climbing aboard is killed ($8B37); a closed barracks (of the first three) within 24 dots right of its X is opened ($8B4B). In front of the ground's depth: a tank within 10 rows of depth and 13 dots is destroyed ($8930).
The blast's search of the tank list.
The helicopter is hit ($10 = 1); the object that hit it is marked 4.

Takes the current object off the drone list.
Takes the current object off the jet list.

The shot that hit the jet.
A drone hit by a shot: the same three bursts as a jet's, and the drone list loses it.
The destroyed drone's place in the drone list.
The shot that hit the drone.
A hostage caught in a blast: its slot freed, one more killed (the counter and its tune), one fewer out.
A blast at barracks A: if it was closed it is open now ($7311 + A), and its hostages can come out ($62F2).
A jet fires: two missiles (type 4), 8 rows above and 9 below it, at the ground's depth, flying 24 dots a frame the way the jet flies, with the noise of the launch.
The jet that fires or bombs.
The second missile's slot.
A jet drops a bomb (type 5) just below it, at the ground's depth, moving 20 dots a frame the way the jet flies.

Three or more blocks from the helicopter it is dropped. Its horizontal speed turns a dot a frame towards the helicopter, to 5 at most, and on the screen its height closes on the helicopter's a dot a frame. At level 3, one time in four when its spin is at the first picture, on the screen and lower than 88, it drops a shell (type 8) moving 10 dots a frame faster or slower than itself.
